notes: Concerns validity of a saloon/liquor-license zoning ordinance under a city charter; no lodging, boarding, or room-letting is at issue.
Disorderly-house prosecution for unlicensed liquor sales; lease evidence goes only to defendant's tenancy/control of the building, not to any lodging/room-letting arrangement.

holding_summary: The court affirmed a conviction for keeping a bawdy house, holding the indictment properly charged the offense in conjunctive form and was not duplicitous, and that evidence was ample even though defendant claimed the women were only lodgers/roomers in his rooming house. The court found the evidence of guilt clear and convincing despite defendant's account of running an ordinary furnished-rooms business.

quotes.text: I rented out my rooms to both regular and transient fbbmers, and some for light house-keeping purposes
The evidence showing the appellant’s guilt is ample, clear and convincing.
After I made the complaint, Cabiness, the defendant, came to me and acknowledged that it was a house of prostitution, and he 'said that he could not make a living by keeping respectable people there.

notes: Defendant ran a rooming-house business (soliciting roomers at the depot, furnished-rooms cards) that was recharacterized as a bawdy house due to prostitutes among the occupants; treated as adverse data on the vulnerability of room-letting operations to nuisance/police-power prosecution.
Pandering/procuring-for-prostitution conviction; 'private boarding house' and 'Rooming House' are only incidental travel-lodging references, not an adjudicated letting arrangement.
Gaming-law case turning on whether a residence remained 'occupied by a family' during a temporary absence; no paying occupant or letting arrangement is involved.

holding_summary: The court reversed a disorderly-house conviction, holding the trial court erred by failing to charge on accomplice testimony where the State's key witness was herself an accomplice. It further held the evidence insufficient because it showed only that appellant kept a boarding house with boarders, without establishing her legal relation (lessee or tenant) to the premises.

quotes.text: There is evidence that she kept a boarding house and had boarders.
Outside of this there is no testimony that shows she was the lessee or tenant.
With the exception in the most inferential way, the evidence is silent as to her relations to the house.

notes: Reversal rests on evidentiary insufficiency in a bawdy/disorderly-house prosecution of a boarding-house keeper, not a substantive ruling protecting or condemning room-letting itself; hence coded mixed.

holding_summary: The court held unconstitutional a Texarkana ordinance criminalizing men and women 'associating together for immoral purposes,' whose provisions swept in any male and female found together in the bedroom of any hotel, rooming house, boarding house, lodging house, or inn, or registering there as man and wife. The ordinance was found overbroad, penalizing innocent conduct (doctors, relatives, delivery agents), and the relator was discharged.

quotes.text: its terms are too broad and many of its sections make penal acts and persons which and who by no construction could be held to be crimes or criminals, and against whose inclusion as such, reason and common sense would revolt.
The ordinance in question being unconstitutional, it would follow that the arrest and conviction of relator was without authority of law, and Ms discharge will be ordered.

notes: characterization left null: this is a facial constitutional challenge to a citywide morals ordinance, not an adjudication of any specific letting/lodging arrangement's legal character. Favorable in that it invalidates police-power regulation reaching hotel/rooming/boarding/lodging-house occupants.
Gaming-law case on whether a wife's temporary absence destroys a residence's 'occupied by a family' status; no compensated occupancy or letting arrangement is at issue.
Concerns an occupation-tax and distance-zoning ordinance for tent shows/carnivals; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.
Concerns a statute against night-time removal of agricultural laborers/tenants from a plantation; not about letting rooms or dwellings for compensated occupancy.
Fire-insurance dispute over the meaning of 'vacant' versus 'occupied' building-use warranties; no lodging or room-letting is involved.
Concerns priority of an irrigation-company statutory lien over a tenant farmer's crops; unrelated to lodging or room-letting.

Strikes down a Dallas ordinance restricting construction of business houses in residence districts; concerns the right to build/use property for business, not the letting of rooms or dwellings to occupants.
Lower-court companion to the Spann v. City of Dallas Supreme Court case (later reversed); same subject, the zoning of business-house construction, not lodging/room-letting.
Concerns municipal segregation of bawdyhouses/red-light district and standing to enjoin them absent special damage; addresses prostitution regulation, not letting of rooms or dwellings for lodging.
Dispute over the constitutionality and scope of a statutory agricultural landlord's lien for crop advances; unrelated to lodging or room-letting.
Workers'-compensation lump-sum award dispute; the widow's running of a rooming house is cited only as a hardship fact, with no legal treatment of the letting arrangement.
Parallel S.W. Reporter version of Stallings v. State (also reported at 75 Tex. Crim. 44); same gaming/family-occupancy exemption issue, no paying occupant or letting arrangement involved.
